public-good.definition: a product that costs its maker something and benefits others nearby, such as an enzyme or iron-scavenging molecule a microbe releases into its surroundings
public-good.excludes: products the maker keeps for itself

producer-cheater.definition: a producer pays a cost to make the public good; a cheater makes none and still gains from the goods of producers near it
producer-cheater.excludes: any intention on either side; the words name two fixed strategies

torus-grid.definition: a square grid whose opposite edges are joined, so every cell has the same number of neighbours and there is no border
torus-grid.excludes: grids with edges, where border cells have fewer neighbours

fitness-proportional.definition: the update rule in which a cell's next occupant is copied from a parent drawn with chance in proportion to the parent's fitness, here among the 3 by 3 window around the cell including the cell itself
fitness-proportional.excludes: other update rules, such as death followed by birth from neighbours only, or imitation of the best neighbour

synchronous.definition: every cell of the grid is replaced at once in each generation, from the fitnesses of the previous generation
synchronous.excludes: asynchronous updating, where one cell at a time is replaced

goods-box.definition: the square of cells over which one producer's goods are spread, 3 by 3 at range 1 and 5 by 5 at range 2
goods-box.excludes: the 3 by 3 window from which parents are drawn, which stays fixed

self-benefit.definition: the part of a producer's own goods that returns to the producer itself; with a 3 by 3 box a producer keeps a ninth of what it makes
self-benefit.excludes: benefit from the goods of other producers, including relatives

bc-ratio.definition: the benefit b that one producer's goods give in total divided by the cost c it pays, written b/c
bc-ratio.excludes: the net payoff to any one cell, which also depends on its neighbours

mixed-arm.definition: the version of the model in which every cell gains from the producer share of the whole population and parents are drawn from the whole population, so neighbours mean nothing

shuffled-arm.definition: the version of the model in which all positions are shuffled at random before each generation and the local rules then apply, so neighbours are strangers
shuffled-arm.excludes: the clustering of relatives that the local arm allows

mean-field.definition: an exact formula for next generation's producer share in the mixed arm, used here as a known answer the simulation must match
mean-field.excludes: the local and shuffled arms, which have no such formula

local-competition.field: social evolution, after Taylor and after Griffin and colleagues
local-competition.definition: competition for space or resources among neighbours, which, when neighbours are relatives, can cancel the benefit that helping relatives brings
local-competition.excludes: competition spread over the whole population

final-share.definition: the share of producers in the grid at the end of a run, averaged over the replicate runs; a run stops early when one type takes the whole grid
final-share.excludes: the share of runs in which producers survived
